question.text: Will criminal or civil immigration charges be brought against Ilhan Omar before 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2027, any criminal charge or civil enforcement action relating to her immigration or citizenship is publicly filed against Ilhan Omar by a US government authority in a federal or state court in the United States.
question.fine_print: This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46452) which opened on 2026-11-09 18:00:00.

research:
I've finished the research and am writing up the findings. One limit: the Star Tribune article came back with HTTP 429, so its claims rest only on the provided news summary and a search snippet.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data series. The question resolves Yes only if a criminal charge or civil enforcement action about Omar's immigration or citizenship is publicly filed in a federal or state court. In practice that means an indictment, a criminal complaint or a civil denaturalization complaint, which would show up on court dockets or in DOJ press releases. I found no such filing as of 2026-11-16.
- 2026-10 to 11: The only court activity tied to Omar is about the search warrant. Chief Judge Boasberg (D.D.C.) is deciding whether to unseal it. Magistrate Judge Sharbaugh signed it. Omar's lawyers have asked for her seized property back. None of this is a charge. [Western Journal](https://www.westernjournal.com/obama-appointed-judge-trump-labeled-lunatic-gets-assigned-ilhan-omars-case/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/17/ilhan-omars-lawyers-demand-the-return-of-property-seized-in-house-raid)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. As of mid-November 2026, Omar has not been charged and no denaturalization case has been filed. [MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/11/03/ilhan-omar-wins-fifth-term-as-federal-investigation-continues)
- 2026-11-03: In court filings, government attorneys said agents had not finished executing the search warrant and that any charges would come after that is complete. No timeline was given. [MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/11/03/ilhan-omar-wins-fifth-term-as-federal-investigation-continues)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: The Star Tribune reports that during Trump's first term, Minnesota federal prosecutors closed an immigration-fraud inquiry into Omar without charges, because the statute of limitations had passed. The current probe is being run from Washington, and Minnesota prosecutors reportedly have no role. I could not verify this directly (HTTP 429). [Star Tribune](https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-prosecutors-closed-an-ilhan-omar-inquiry-washington-is-investigating-again/601917573)
- 2026-11-15: A Hot Air opinion piece, by the author of a book attacking Omar, argues that denaturalization is possible. It is partisan, not news. [Hot Air](https://hotair.com/headlines/2026/11/15/the-case-against-ilhan-omar-n3821004)
- 2026-11-11 to 13 (New York Times, via GV Wire): This is about Abdullahi Mohamed, who briefly worked as Omar's bodyguard.
  - In March 2026, prosecutors in Minneapolis questioned him at a proffer session about Omar's immigration history and a $10,000 payment.
  - In April he was indicted for lying under oath.
  - On 2026-09-03 he testified with immunity before a Washington grand jury that is reviewing the Omar case.
  - The next day, prosecutors moved to dismiss his indictment, and he left the US.
  - His lawyer says a prosecutor told him the probe was "100% being run by 1600 Pennsylvania Ave." DOJ calls the case "completely unrelated."
  
  [GV Wire/NYT](https://gvwire.com/?p=277487), [Common Dreams](https://www.commondreams.org/news/ilhan-omar-bodyguard)
- 2026-11-03: Omar won a fifth term while the investigation continued. [MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/11/03/ilhan-omar-wins-fifth-term-as-federal-investigation-continues)
- 2026-10-28: DOJ refused to release the search warrant, calling the investigation active. [MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/10/28/ilhan-omar-search-warrant-will-not-be-released-by-the-justice-department)
- 2026-10-19: Former prosecutor Jonathan Fahey said civil denaturalization is the more likely route, because the 10-year criminal limit for conduct tied to her 2000 naturalization has probably run out. [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/nation-world/omar-denies-any-fraud-blasts-probe-as-a-political-hit-job-as-scrutiny-widens-trump-administration-immigration-jonathan-fahey-somalia-minnesota-representative-democrat-congress-denaturalization-government-washington-dc)
- 2026-10-13/14: About a dozen grand jury subpoenas went out, including to Omar's sister Sahra Noor. AP says they are tied to a grand jury in Minnesota, which conflicts with the Washington grand jury in the NYT report. Omar herself was not subpoenaed. Her phone was seized. [PBS/AP](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/ap-report-rep-ilhan-omars-phone-seized-and-relatives-subpoenaed-in-criminal-probe), [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2026/10/14/doj-subpoenas-ilhan-omar/)
- 2026-10-17: Omar's lawyers say agents ignored the magistrate's limits on the search, including a requirement to contact the House General Counsel, and demanded her property back. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/17/ilhan-omars-lawyers-demand-the-return-of-property-seized-in-house-raid)
- Early October 2026: DHS agents searched her D.C. home.

## 4. Base rates
- Legal limits:
  - Criminal naturalization fraud (18 U.S.C. § 1425) generally has a 10-year limitations period.
  - Civil denaturalization has no statute of limitations, and the government must prove its case by "clear, convincing, and unequivocal" evidence. [CRS](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/LSB11437.html)
  - Some academics argue the 5-year default limit in 28 U.S.C. § 2462 should apply to civil denaturalization, but courts have rejected that argument. [Northwestern L. Rev.](https://northwesternlawreview.org/?p=8210)
  - Newer conduct, such as false statements in 2016 or later, or financial disclosures, could still be charged criminally. Only charges about immigration or citizenship count for this question.
- Indictments of sitting members of Congress are rare, roughly 0 to 2 a year historically. I found no precedent for a member being denaturalized.
- Timing: the search was in early October and agents had not finished executing the warrant as of early November. Seizing devices from a member of Congress usually brings Speech or Debate review, which tends to take months. That is an inference, not something a source states.

- Polymarket "US files Omar denaturalization case by Dec 31": 5.85%. By Mar 31, 2027: 7.5%.
- Kalshi "US move to revoke Omar's citizenship before 2027": 11%. Kalshi "citizenship revoked before 2027": 3%.
- Polymarket "Omar arrested by Dec 31": 6.5%. "Deported by Dec 31, 2026": 1.5%.
- I found no expert forecasts. The Metaculus community figure for question 46452 was not available.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2027-01-01
- DOJ finishing execution of the search warrant, which the government said must come before any charges.
- Boasberg's ruling on unsealing the warrant and affidavit, and any ruling on Omar's motion to return her property.
- More grand jury activity: testimony from subpoenaed relatives, or a possible indictment.
- DOJ deciding between a criminal case and a civil denaturalization filing. The civil route avoids the limitations problem the Star Tribune describes.
- Political signals from Trump, Homan or DOJ leadership. Separately, House GOP inquiries into Omar's finances and a possible expulsion vote (Kalshi: 4% before 2027) would not count for this question.

- **Criminal route:** Naturalization fraud generally carries a 10-year limitations window from naturalization, and she naturalized in 2000. Some former prosecutors say a conspiracy charge (18 U.S.C. 371) could still work if an overt act happened in the last five years. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/17/politics/explainer-wouldnt-be-easy-to-strip-rep-ilhan-omar-citizenship)

- **Timing:** The search was on Oct 12, so about six more weeks before the deadline would make roughly 11 weeks from search to charge. That is short for a sealed, politically sensitive case involving a sitting member of Congress, especially with a Speech or Debate Clause filter process in place. I found no systematic data on how long search-to-indictment takes for members of Congress.
- I found no precedent of the federal government filing a denaturalization case against a sitting member of Congress.

(a) About 6.5 weeks remain, until January 1, 2027. Yes requires a US government authority to publicly file, in a federal or state court, a criminal charge (indictment or complaint) or a civil enforcement action (for example a denaturalization complaint) against Omar that relates to her immigration or citizenship.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of November 16 nothing has been filed, the search warrant is sealed, and on November 3 the government said agents had not finished executing it and that any charges would come only after that.

(c) Base rate: indictments of sitting members of Congress are rare, roughly 0 to 2 a year. Conditional on an active, publicly known federal probe with a search already executed, the chance of charges within the next roughly 6 weeks is historically low, about 5-10%. Search-to-indictment for members of Congress usually takes many months, partly because of Speech or Debate filter review. Liquid markets anchor higher:
- Polymarket "federally charged by Dec 31": 22%.
- Kalshi federal charge: 24%.
- Denaturalization filing: Polymarket 6%, Kalshi "move to revoke" 11%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The probe is run from Washington, and a lawyer says it is "100% being run by 1600 Pennsylvania Ave," which signals political will.
- A grand jury is active, with about a dozen subpoenas around October 13-21, the bodyguard's testimony on September 3, and her phone seized.
- NBC reported on October 21 that possible charges are conspiracy and false statements.
- Civil denaturalization has no statute of limitations.
- The administration has been willing to move fast against political opponents.

Evidence for No:
- Warrant execution was still incomplete as of November 3.
- Speech or Debate review is likely.
- The Star Tribune (November 16) reports that Minnesota prosecutors earlier closed an inquiry because the statute of limitations had run out.
- The window is short, and late December holidays slow filings.
- The evidentiary bar for denaturalization is high.

(e) No scenario: the filter review and fights over unsealing the warrant drag into 2027, and DOJ keeps building the case or quietly stalls after the midterms.

Yes scenario: political pressure from the White House leads DOJ to have the D.C. grand jury return a conspiracy or false-statement indictment in December, or to file a civil denaturalization complaint, which avoids the limitations problem.

(f) I start from the market cluster. Federal-charge markets at 22-24% include non-immigration charges, such as the Pirro finance probe, which do not count here. Civil filings count here but add only a little beyond the overlap. That gives a net of about 20% implied. I shade down to about 15% for three reasons: the government itself says the warrant is not fully executed, the window is short with holidays, and markets on politically charged prosecutions tend to overprice Yes. I keep a meaningful tail because this administration has charged opponents abruptly before.

Probability: 15%
